data.title: Jakarta airport extends closure after volcano eruption
data.description: JAKARTA - Jakarta's main airport and three others delayed reopening on Monday after halting operations due to a volcanic eruption and leaving hundreds of thousands stranded.

data.title: AI data centers are less thirsty now, tech giants say
data.description: NEW YORK - Data centers are running into a wall of public anger in the United States over their thirst for water and power.

data.title: North Korea vows nuclear-armed navy as US ally drills open
data.description: SEOUL - Leader Kim Jong Un vowed to build North Korea's navy into a nuclear-armed force, state media reported Monday as US allies' maritime drills were to begin.

data.title: 'Trumpapalooza' tests Republican bet on unpopular US president
data.description: WASHINGTON (UNITED STATES) - US Republicans will gather in Dallas, Texas, next week for a two-day convention aimed at convincing voters that Donald Trump is effectively on the ballot in November -- even as the deeply unpopular president threatens to become a liability for his own party.

data.title: 25 years on, America seeks to keep 9/11 memories alive
data.description: NEW YORK - A quarter century after the era-defining attacks of September 11, the United States is eager to keep alive the memory of a 2001 trauma that is fading as the proportion of Americans who did not experience it firsthand grows.

data.title: Five dead, five injured after Amazon cargo plane overshoots Miami runway
data.description: MIAMI - At least five people were killed when an Amazon cargo plane overshot a runway after it landed Sunday at Miami International Airport, crashed into vehicles and caught fire, officials said.

data.title: More than 140 killed in latest Yemen clashes: military sources
data.description: TAIZ (YEMEN) - Fighting between Yemeni government forces and Iran-backed Houthi rebels in southwest Yemen killed more than 140 combatants between midday Saturday and early Sunday morning, military sources said.

data.title: Lebanon president calls for US help as Israeli strikes kill 7
data.description: ARABSALIM (LEBANON) - Lebanese President Joseph Aoun urged Washington and the international community to help stop Israeli attacks, which killed at least seven people on Sunday despite a truce and a framework deal aimed at halting the violence.

data.title: Amazon cargo plane overshoots Miami runway, hits vehicles, catches fire
data.description: MIAMI - An Amazon cargo plane overshot a runway as it landed Sunday in Miami, crashing into vehicles and catching fire, officials said.

data.title: German AfD supporters jubilant at far right's thumping win
data.description: MAGDEBURG (GERMANY) - Letting out cries of joy and jumping into the air, supporters of Germany's far-right AfD celebrated as they realised the scale of their election triumph in an ex-communist eastern state on Sunday.

data.title: 'Truly scared': Blazes outpace firefighters in Indonesian Borneo
data.description: PONTIANAK (INDONESIA) - Toiling around the clock, haggard Indonesian firefighters on Borneo island cannot keep up with the blazes devouring landscapes and shrouding communities in a cloying haze.

data.title: Iran threatens greater force if US launches more attacks
data.description: TEHRAN - Iran's top negotiator on Sunday threatened a more forceful response to any further US attacks after Tehran targeted American warships in their latest round of clashes.

data.title: Nepali rescuers buoyed by miracle finds but tough conditions persist
data.description: KATHMANDU - Nepali rescuers faced challenging conditions on Sunday as search operations after catastrophic floods entered their 12th day, buoyed by the extraordinary rescues of four survivors.

data.title: Indonesia's main airport suspends flights as Krakatoa erupts
data.description: JAKARTA - Indonesia halted operations at its main international airport outside Jakarta on Sunday after ash spewed from the Anak Krakatoa volcano more than 150 kilometres away, impacting thousands of passengers.

data.title: US aircraft carrier departs Thailand after port call
data.description: LAEM CHABANG (THAILAND) - Thousands of US sailors aboard an aircraft carrier departed from Thailand on Sunday, AFP journalists said, concluding its first port call following reports of deteriorating living conditions on board after nine months at sea.

data.title: China's memories of Mao fade to nostalgia 50 years after his death
data.description: NANJIE (CHINA) - The crimson flags on Nanjie village's "East is Red" Square hang limp in the sweltering summer heat as a trickle of tourists take photos with a towering statue of Chairman Mao Zedong, still gleaming white almost 50 years after he died.

data.title: US envoys discuss 'substantive' plan with Putin towards ending Ukraine war
data.description: KYIV - American envoys discussed "substantive plan" for next steps to end the Ukraine war during their meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin, the White House said, before they headed to Kyiv on Sunday.

data.title: 'The flood is coming': How a Nepal principal saved 900 students
data.description: NUWAKOT (NEPAL) - Rajendra Dawadi was inside his school near Nepal's Trishuli River with around 900 students last week when a colleague delivered an urgent warning.

data.title: Argentina threatens to sanction oil projects around Falklands
data.description: BUENOS AIRES (ARGENTINA) - Argentina has announced that it will investigate and sanction oil companies working near the Falkland Islands without authorization, after President Javier Milei said the "winds of change" favor his country's claim to the archipelago.

data.title: Prince William to represent King Charles III at Norway late King Harald's funeral
data.description: LONDON - Britain's Prince William will attend the funeral of Norway's late King Harald next week in place of his father King Charles III, Buckingham Palace said on Saturday.

data.title: US envoy says Israel has responsibility for Palestinians
data.description: TURMUS AYYA, Palestinian Territories - The US ambassador to Israel said on Saturday that the Israeli government bore responsibility for West Bank Palestinians’ safety and should impose “severe consequences” over violence, as he visited families after a surge in settler attacks.

data.title: Commemoration held for Serbian war criminal Mladic
data.description: BELGRADE - A commemoration was held on Saturday in Belgrade for war criminal Ratko Mladic two days ahead of his burial, attended by dozens of former military personnel, family members and officials.

data.title: Russia hits Kyiv airports as Trump envoys awaited
data.description: KYIV - Russian strikes hit Kyiv’s airports overnight, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said on Saturday, as US envoys arrived in Moscow to discuss a plan to end more than four years of war.

data.title: Global autonomous weapons pact taking shape
data.description: GENEVA - The ⁠128 ⁠states party to ​a framework that regulates or bans weapons considered as indiscriminate, ​or causing too many ‌injuries, have agreed on a document that could pave the way to international rules on autonomous weapons.

data.title: Masked anti-migrant protesters shut down UK port
data.description: Dozens of masked people reportedly protesting against Channel migrant crossings blocked access to the Port of Dover in southern England on Saturday, halting traffic that is ferried between France and the UK.
